entries.name: Fred Shuttlesworth

expected.charges: Vagrancy and aiding and abetting others to break the law — arrested March 31, 1960.
expected.sentence:
180 days at hard labor plus a $100 fine. Actual time served is not documented; the conviction was overturned.

Verdict as recorded: Yes — convicted April 4, 1960; the conviction was reversed by the U.S. Supreme Court in 1963.

Charges as recorded: Vagrancy and aiding and abetting others to break the law — arrested March 31, 1960 during the Birmingham sit-in campaign and again on April 2 (Shuttlesworth & Billups v. City of Birmingham).

entries.rationale: National Guardian, April 18, 1960, page 8 reports March 31 arrest, overnight jail and release on bond the next day. Replace sentence-derived September 27 endpoint for this first detention. A separate April 2 rearrest is reported; its endpoint remains unresolved and must not be merged into continuous six-month custody.

entries.rationale: LDF Supreme Court petitioner brief, October Term 1963 No.168, printed pages4 and7 (PDF10 and13), dates arrest May17,1961 and transport to city jail.
